label: late original-phase input of d/r/m/a/b/s/l (long sequences), few such letters earlier
explanation: Fires only near the end of the original phase in long sequences: t=5-8 (95% of mass, rate climbing to 19% at orig_idx 8; 60% of mass at the last original token) and weakly on <DEL> (5%); never at t<=3 and never in the copy phase; L>=8 holds 90% of mass. Within those positions it is strongly token-selective: inputs d, r, m, a, b, s, l (lift 2.6-5x; d strongest) carry ~80% of mass, with weaker i/k/w/p/y. It is suppressed when such letters already occurred earlier in the sequence (in_first=1 holds 87% of mass) and enhanced when the sequence starts with e/t/c/3/v (first_tok lift ~2.5-3x), so it looks like a context-gated late-input detector rather than a clean token feature. Top activations (max) are d/r on the final original step of length-8/9 sequences. The positional+token rule (t>=5, in_tok in set) gets mass recall 0.81 but precision only 0.23; adding the history condition raises dev F1 to ~0.46 at the cost of recall. Magnitude rises with position (later steps / last original token) and is highest for d and r.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: d, r, m, a, b, s; least: j, t, 2, u) and the first original token (most: e, t, c, v, 3, u; least: m, r, d, b); timing cues that raise it most: t=7, t=8, L=9 & t=8.
